# Ariadne

> Ariadne is a local-first multilingual memory server for Codex, Claude Code, and any MCP client.

## Core facts

- Project site: https://mclaut.github.io/ariadne/
- Hugging Face Space: https://huggingface.co/spaces/mclaut/ariadne
- Source and documentation: https://github.com/mclaut/ariadne
- Latest release: https://github.com/mclaut/ariadne/releases/latest
- License: MIT
- Platforms: Windows x64, macOS Intel and Apple Silicon, Linux x64 and ARM64
- Runtime: Go MCP server, Qdrant vector server, Ollama bge-m3 embeddings
- Retrieval: exact lookup by ID or hybrid dense plus BM25 sparse search, with wing, room, and collection scopes plus bounded historical-intent reranking
- MCP tools: memory_save, memory_recall, memory_delete, memory_move, credential_access
- Privacy: local endpoints by default; Qdrant binds to 127.0.0.1; project scope is default-deny; cross-wing recall requires a visible human approval
- Lifecycle: scoped append-only identities retain superseded and orphaned history for exact-ID audit
- Maintenance: incremental memfile sync, guarded diary consolidation, bounded retries, and append-only health activity
- Token efficiency: confirmed savings, recall overhead, and signed net are measured locally without storing content

## Install

Windows uses install.ps1. Linux and macOS use install.sh. Both are available in the repository root.

## Current release

v0.8.6 fixes launchd-supervised tray restarts and service-error propagation, reduces system approval warnings to deliberate Approve/Deny clicks with no default keyboard action, and keeps Claude's project recall current across startup, resume, clear, compact, and fork. The installer now repairs stale Ariadne skills and hooks without replacing unrelated Claude entries. v0.8.5 brought the native macOS warning to the foreground. v0.8.3 introduced scoped cross-wing and separate one-shot credential grants, while v0.8.2 made project scope default-deny and added secret blocking plus append-only quarantine. The approval handshake is audited agent policy, not an operating-system credential broker.
